summary:
I found no path by which the logic RNG gets drawn at display rate. This is static analysis only. It covers 307 direct call sites in 192 functions. It is based on a direct-call graph plus a root-class analysis; a few virtual edges are still unresolved.

The build has three separate RNG streams:
- logic: dword_CB0220[6]
- client: dword_CB01F0[6]
- audio: dword_CB0208[6]

All three are advanced by sub_6008D0. None of the logic wrappers (sub_600A80, sub_600B10, sub_600CF0) is referenced by a pointer.

Lua is split cleanly between two states:
- The logic Lua state (TheLuaScriptEngine = dword_CDD17C, field +36) holds GetRandomNumber (sub_555DF0 → sub_600B10(0,1), logic RNG) and ObjectTestCanSufferFear (sub_578CF0 → sub_600A80, logic RNG).
- The drawable Lua state (field +40, which runs ScriptedModelDraw <Script> blocks through sub_572EB0 from sub_90D620) holds only the CurDrawable* functions, GetFrame and GetClientRandomNumberReal (sub_555D00 → sub_600B60, client RNG). GetRandomNumber is not registered there.

The only bridge from draw code into the logic Lua state is the ScriptedModelDraw LuaEvent firer, sub_8F34F0 → sub_5A2950(TheLuaScriptEngine, 15, …). It can never fire:
- At 0x8F34F8 it returns immediately when the event count at [+0x78] is above zero.
- Its loop bound is [+0x7C] + 16*[+0x78], so with a count of zero it does nothing.
If it were live, it would be exactly the feared hazard: sub_903020 fires ON_FRAME events on every draw where (int)anim frame == Frame, with no previous-frame dedupe. That would fire about 2× at 60 fps and 3× at 90 fps.

XML check:
- Official RA3 XML (full grep): no GetRandomNumber, GetClientRandomNumber, math.random, <LuaEvent or ObjectTestCanSufferFear.
- Remix tree: only scripts.lua lines 258 and 279 (ObjectTestCanSufferFear, inside logic fear-event handlers).
- scripts.lua and scriptevents.xml contain no "random" at all.

Reachability from display code:
- Forward closure from the hub sub_542DF0, draw sub_5D9A50, view sub_5EB7D0 / sub_5EB5E0 and every slot of the resolved hub-manager vtables (2697 functions) reaches no logic-RNG draw. It only reaches a one-shot game-start reseed: sub_542DF0 → sub_4E0B90, guarded by the this[198] flag.
- Sweeps of the UI, client and draw address ranges find only a UI loading-screen path that never reaches the draw (a4=0), map-load paths, and two sim-side functions that live in the draw address range: the W3DDynamicsDraw helper that picks logic or client RNG by a flag (draw callers pass 0 = client), and a logic update module.
- The predecessor's root classification of all 192 logic-RNG callers shows only sim classes. No draw module (mask 1024), client update (2048) or client behavior (4096) is a root.

All logic subsystem updates live in GameLogic slot 13, sub_4F81F0(phase), gated by phase: phase 1 runs ScriptEngine, LuaScriptEngine and AI, the heavy RNG users. It is called only from sub_616130 (dump 451093/451104), which is the block the patch's scheduler replaces.

So in this dimension, vanilla's determinism does not depend on r being fixed. What matters is that each phase 1..6 runs exactly once per logic frame. The phase schedule is therefore the RNG-relevant suspect for "source I (FL_G_RATIO only)". The logic-RNG CRC (sub_600950) is part of the sync CRC in sub_4D7F40, so any extra draw shows up quickly.

Two minor leads outside RNG proper:
- Lua math.random uses CRT rand(), which network code seeds from GetTickCount. It is unused by stock and Remix data.
- A logic update module (update at 0x8E3180) copies a dynamics-body transform into the Object position. Whether that body is stepped per display frame is unverified.

verified.title: No logic-RNG consumer is reachable from display-rate code; logic RNG use is phase-gated inside GameLogic slot 13 (sub_4F81F0), driven only by sub_616130
verified.mechanism: Forward direct-call closure from sub_542DF0, sub_5D9A50, sub_5EB7D0, sub_5EB5E0 and all slots of the resolved hub-manager vtables (2697 functions) contains no logic-RNG draw. It only contains the one-shot game-start path sub_542DF0 -> sub_4E0B90 (if this[198]) -> sub_600A30(*(dword_CE3A78+76)) or sub_600970(0). Address-range sweeps (UI 0xA80000-0xB20000, client 0x5B8000-0x5F0000, draw 0x8E0000-0x920000) found only map-load chains (root sub_5BA760, W3DTerrainLogic), a loading-screen path that never reaches the RNG (RNG-7), W3DDynamicsDraw helpers that draw callers use in client mode, and a logic update module (RNG-6). The reverse root classification of all 192 callers gives only sim classes. The logic subsystems (ScriptEngine CDD190, LuaScriptEngine CDD17C and AI CE8F60 in phase 1; others in phases 2/3-6/5) are updated in sub_4F81F0(this, phase), whose only caller is sub_616130 (the batch loop the patch replaces at P2 0x0061626E). Per logic frame, RNG consumption therefore depends only on which phases run, not on display fps. Vanilla r=2 is deterministic in this dimension because each logic frame runs phases 1..6 exactly once (3 per client frame), not because draws are counted. The residual risk sits in the patched scheduler: if it ever calls sub_4F81F0 with a repeated or skipped phase when r=4 or 6, phase-1 work (script actions sub_5AE1A0/58AF90/58B390, AIPlayer) consumes a different number of logic draws. That would fit 'source I only with FL_G_RATIO'.

corrections:
1) Correction to "Vanilla r=2 is deterministic because each logic frame runs phases 1..6 exactly once". This does not hold under a time freeze. In sub_4F81F0 phase 1 (0x4F8342-0x4F8366), when v4 is set (tactical-view freeze or ScriptEngine sub_5571F0) and sub_6003A0(1) fails (ECX = dword_CE2FBC, which checks the command list for a type-1 message), the function sets CDB750+196 = 0 and returns. The batch loop in sub_616130 (dump 451100-451105) still runs phases 2 and 3, and sub_6027D0 restores this[22] so phase 1 is retried on the next client frame. So during a freeze, vanilla re-runs phases 2-3 on every client frame. The patch re-runs only phase 2 at r=4 (fl_target_phase(1,4)=2) and nothing at r=6. Because the per-client-frame re-run is r-dependent, this is a way the phase counts can differ in vanilla too. The Zero Hour source says this path should never happen in a network game, so it is probably low risk for multiplayer, but replays or scripted freezes could see it. Whether a phase-3 re-run (object module bucket 0 at this+220) draws from the logic RNG is speculative. Check whether the modules in bucket 0 are skipped when re-entered in the same logic frame (the bucket loop is at dump 212960+).

2) The logic-RNG consumers are more exactly: sub_600A80, sub_600B10 and sub_600CF0 (wrappers on 0xCB0220), plus sub_613160 and sub_61B770, which use 0xCB0220 directly and are called only from sub_61BBB0 at map start.

3) The direct-call part of the closure is 1,601 functions. The finding's figure of 2,697 includes virtual calls resolved through vtables. The objects in the hub's vector at this+4 (vtbl+20 loop, dump 279653) are not resolved statically, so this remains a gap.

4) Suggested fix: the proposed assert (sub_4F81F0 runs once per phase per logic frame) should also count the calls made while CDB750+196 == 0 after phase 1.

1. Evidence item 'dump 212814: the only virtual call through dword_CDD17C is +20' is narrowly true but incomplete. The logic Lua state is also entered by direct calls: sub_5A2950 -> sub_5A0060 from many object-range functions, and from the draw-range functions sub_903020, sub_90C1B0 and sub_90D620 via sub_8F34F0. The draw-range route is dead code (0x8F34F8: 'cmp [eax+0x78],0 / ja 0x8F360E', and the loop bound is the same count), so the conclusion still holds. Add this to ruled_out.
2. Drawable AnimationState <Script> Lua (sub_90D620 -> sub_572EB0) runs in state CDD17C+40 (sub_582930). That state has only GetClientRandomNumberReal (client stream) and no GetRandomNumber. Add this to ruled_out as well.
3. The residual-risk hypothesis ('repeated or skipped phase at r=4/6 would fit source I') is not supported by the scheduler math in src/schedule.h. fl_target_phase(p,r)+1 is the upper bound of the batch loop (fl_hook_batch, framelab.cpp:1388). For r=4 it yields client frames {1,2},{3},{4,5},{6}; for r=6, one phase each. This assumes sub_6027D0 advances this[22] by exactly one per client frame and wraps after 6, which is unverified.
4. 'Per logic frame RNG consumption depends only on which phases run' overstates the case. Sim branches that read display-dependent state, such as the patched derived globals CDBC50, CDBC54, CDBC5C and CDBD34, could change how many draws are made. That belongs to a different dimension and does not refute reachability.
5. The one-shot reseed flag CDB750+198, consumed in sub_542DF0 at dump 279868, is set only by sub_AB6B00. That function has no direct callers, and a pointer to it is stored in .rdata at 0xC8110C (a UI or interface callback table). When the reseed lands relative to the first logic phase is unverified; this is an open lead, not a refutation.

Drop the scheduler repeat/skip hypothesis. P2/P3 plus sub_6027D0 structurally guarantee that phases 1..6 each run exactly once per logic frame at r=2, 4 and 6 (and P7 is off by default). Put the r-dependent risk at the display-rate deferred transform flush instead:
sub_6027D0 -> vtbl+148 sub_626620 (every client frame, before the phase dispatch) -> sub_4D5600 @0x6266F7 (runs once per client frame after any sub_4F81F0 phase call, because sub_4F81F0 clears GameLogic+796 each phase, dump 212756) -> sub_7C2670 @0x4D560C -> sub_79E800(obj,...,flag=2) @0x7C26B4.
When an object moved more than 0.01 since the snapshot, the flag-2 branch calls obj vtbl+0x18 and contain(+0x328/+0x32C) vtbl+0x14, and sets DynamicsUpdate(obj+0x390)+0x39 = 1. This logic-module state changes at a cadence of r flushes per logic frame (vanilla: before phases 1 and 4; r=4: before 1,3,4,6; r=6: before every phase). The finding's root set (542DF0/5D9A50/5EB7D0/5EB5E0 plus hub-manager vtables) missed sub_6027D0 and sub_626620. The claim should narrow to: no direct-call path from display-rate code draws logic RNG. The only closure hit (via sub_4EE150) needs flag&1, and sub_600AB0 uses client RNG CB01F0. Candidate fix (speculative): gate the sub_4D5600 flush to the vanilla phase boundaries (run it only in client frames whose first phase is 1 or 4). Alternatively, call sub_7C2670 at fixed phases inside the logic schedule so the flush positions relative to phases match r=2 at any r.
refutations:
I checked the finding's two halves separately.

(1) The claimed risk: the patched scheduler repeating or skipping a phase. This cannot happen. sub_6027D0 (dump 433886+) adds exactly 1 to this[22] on each client frame and then calls vtbl+0x90 (= sub_616130; vtable slots 0xBEB618 and 0xC0D648) with v4+1. sub_616130 (dump 451093-451107) calls slot 13 (sub_4F81F0) for a2, then loops v7 = a2+1 .. target, doing ++this[22] for each extra phase. The P2 replacement (framelab.cpp ~2248-2262: push edi; push esi; call fl_hook_batch; mov edi,eax; mov ebx,1; add esi,ebx) sets the loop bound to fl_target_phase(p,r)+1, and that target always lies in [p,6] (schedule.h). For r=4 the phases run as {1,2},{3},{4,5},{6}; for r=6 there is one phase per frame. The unpatched formula at r=4 also runs one contiguous phase per call. When the counter wraps (v4+1==7), this[22] resets to 1, and it reverts to 6 if the frame was not ready. The P7 gate (0x602942) was the only code that ever dropped slot-0x90 calls, and it is out of the default set (framelab.cpp 986-1003). So at any r, each logic frame calls sub_4F81F0 for phases 1..6 exactly once, in order. Through the mechanism the finding proposes, 30/60/90 fps players would draw the same RNG counts. Also, sub_4F81F0 has no direct code refs (refs.py: none). Its only vtable slots are 0xBE9E20 and 0xBEB664, and the only +52 calls on dword_CD8CE4 are at dump 451093 and 451104.

(2) The negative claim. It holds only for direct calls, and the conclusion drawn from it ("RNG use depends only on which phases run, not on display fps") is not established. The root set left out the client-frame loop itself. sub_6027D0 calls vtbl+148 = sub_626620 (0xBEB61C and 0xC0D64C) on every client frame, before the phase dispatch. sub_626620 calls sub_4D5600(TheGameLogic) at 0x6266F7. If byte GameLogic+796 is 0, sub_4D5600 calls sub_7C2670 (0x4D560C). sub_4F81F0 clears +796 unconditionally at the start of every phase call (dump 212756). Each of these is the only call site (full E8/E9 scan of .text). sub_7C2670 empties the double-buffered deferred transform-change list (dword_CE5930/34). sub_7ADF20 (Object setTransform) fills that list after taking a snapshot of the old position/angle, and itself calls sub_79E800 with flag 1. sub_7C2670 calls sub_79E800 with flag 2 (push 2 at 0x7C269E). In the flag-2 branch, when position or angle changed by more than 0.01 since the snapshot, the code:
- calls obj vtbl+0x18 (0x79E8E0);
- calls vtbl+0x14 on the Contain-like module at obj+0x328, or the first entry of the obj+0x32C list (0x79E929);
- executes `mov byte ptr [eax+0x39],1`, where eax = obj+0x390 (0x79E938). obj+0x390 is the cached DynamicsUpdate module pointer (dump 777193, sub_79D530, set when the module name == "DynamicsUpdate"). sub_7ADF20's immediate path never sets this flag.

So the logic-side module state is changed from display-rate code r times per logic frame. The flushes fall before phases 1 and 4 at vanilla r=2, before 1, 3, 4 and 6 at r=4, and before every phase at r=6. Which phase first sees the flag, the contained-rider reposition, and the 0.01 displacement test (a window between flushes, reset each flush through +0x1E4) therefore depends on r. The direct-call closure I built from 0x6027D0 and 0x626620 has 3163 functions. It reaches logic RNG only through sub_79E800 -> sub_4EE150, and that path sits behind the NaN check guarded by flag&1, which is dead for flag 2. The other hit, sub_600AB0, uses client RNG CB01F0. So the narrow statement "no direct display-rate logic-RNG draw" survives. The finding's risk location and its fps-independence conclusion do not.

Whether the DynamicsUpdate flag or contain reaction actually changes sim state is speculative until the reader of +0x39 is checked. This mechanism depends only on r, not on render rate. That fits the measurements: source I appears only with FL_G_RATIO on, and the full patch at 30 fps survived. This fit is speculative.

verified.title: Lua math.random in both Lua states uses CRT rand(), which network code seeds with GetTickCount; unused by stock/Remix data
verified.mechanism: sub_A70420 (luaopen_math, table 0xC7B6E8, 23 entries) is opened in both the logic state (sub_5B06E0) and the drawable state (sub_582930). math.random = sub_A702A0 returns rand() % 0x7FFF scaled; math.randomseed = sub_A703E0 calls srand. The CRT stream is shared by the whole process and time-seeded by the online/network code, so a logic-side script calling math.random would desync even in vanilla, independent of fps. A draw <Script> calling math.random only perturbs that shared CRT stream. No logic-RNG impact.
evidence: binary luaL_reg at 0xC7B790: 'random' -> 0x00A702A0, 0xC7B798: 'randomseed' -> 0x00A703E0

CRT rand/srand sites: sub_93FC20 srand(TickCount) dump 1137289; sub_9553E0 1155650; sub_962E00 1167236; sub_963E90 1167946; sub_982740 1191843; other rand(): sub_63CCB0, sub_6BA950, sub_6BE640, sub_956D30, sub_961D30, sub_964800, sub_96D900, sub_999030, sub_B8B5F0/B8B650
Remix Additional/scripts/scripts.lua and scriptevents.xml: grep -ci random = 0; official XML full grep: 0 'math.random'
verified.fix_proposal: No action for stock or Remix. If mods matter, the patch could rebind math.random in the logic state (TheLuaScriptEngine+36) to a logic-RNG wrapper. That changes behavior, so it should be opt-in.
corrections: Replace 'math.random' / 'math.randomseed' with the Lua 4.0 globals `random` / `randomseed`. sub_A74400 is the Lua 4.0 luaL_openlib (n-counted loop of lua_setglobal), so no `math` table exists. The official-data evidence should be a bare-token grep: both the Remix tree and the official RA3 folder return 0 hits for (^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.:])(random|randomseed)\s*\(. Change 'CRT stream shared by the whole process' to: MSVCR80 rand state is per thread. The GetTickCount srand sites (GameSpy-like, sub_93FC20/9553E0/962E00/963E90/982740) seed whichever thread runs them. Whether that is the main (logic/Lua) thread is unverified (speculative). Add the missing rand callers sub_9400B0 and sub_9827D0. Fix proposal: rebind the global "random" (not math.random) in the logic state (TheLuaScriptEngine this[9]/+36, created in sub_5B06E0). Stock already provides "GetRandomNumber" there (sub_555DF0 -> sub_600B10(0.0,1.0), a logic-RNG real), and "GetClientRandomNumberReal" (sub_555D00 -> sub_600B60) in the drawable state. A wrapper could call sub_600B10 and keep the rest of the random() argument handling.

1. "The CRT stream is shared by the whole process" is wrong. The game imports rand and srand from MSVCR80.dll. In that DLL (WinSxS 8.0.50727.9680), rand is `call _getptd; mov ecx,[eax+0x14]; imul ecx,0x343FD; add ecx,0x269EC3; mov [eax+0x14],ecx; shr 16; and 0x7FFF`, and srand is `call _getptd; mov [eax+0x14],seed`. The seed (_holdrand) is therefore per thread. The GameSpy srand(GetTickCount) calls only reseed the thread that makes them. Both Lua states share the main thread's stream, speculatively, since they are driven from the main/logic thread.

2. The main-thread stream is also consumed at display-frame cadence by client FX code through sub_999030. Its callers include sub_5C5C60, sub_5C9790 and sub_525150. So a hypothetical mod calling math.random in the logic state would desync. The cause would be varying per-machine and per-fps consumption in vanilla, not only the time seed. Recommending against it, or rebinding it opt-in to the logic RNG, is still correct.

3. Minor: "TheLuaScriptEngine+36" is the this[9] slot of the object whose init is sub_5B06E0. I did not independently check the name TheLuaScriptEngine.

1) Wrong name. sub_A70420 is Lua 4.0 lmathlib: 23 entries including 'mod', a PI global and a pow tag method. sub_A74400 (dump 1390133) loops over the entries and calls sub_40A9E0 (pushcclosure) then sub_40ACA0 (setglobal) for each. The functions are therefore the globals `random()` and `randomseed()`, not `math.random`. The 'math.random' grep of official XML proves nothing. A bare `random(` / `randomseed(` grep also comes back zero, so the conclusion still stands.
2) "Shared by the whole process" is wrong. rand and srand are imported from MSVCR80.dll (IAT 0xBC740C and 0xBC744C). In that runtime the rand state is kept per thread (_holdrand). The GetTickCount srand calls (sub_93FC20, sub_9553E0, sub_962E00, sub_963E90, sub_982740) only seed the thread they run on. Whether that is the main thread, where the Lua states run, is unverified (speculative).
3) The mod-hardening fix site would be rebinding the global `random` in the logic state (this[9] of the sub_5B06E0 owner, i.e. +36), not a `math` table entry.
4) The one gameplay-related CRT rand() consumer is sub_63CCB0 (GameInfo reset, this+148 = seed). It runs in the lobby and the seed is distributed (ancestor setSeed), so it is not fps-sensitive.
refutations:
The counterfactual lens asks whether this makes 30, 60 and 90 fps players compute different sim state. It does not. The finding itself says the mechanism is independent of fps and has "no logic-RNG impact". I checked every piece it depends on and found nothing sim-visible at any fps:
(1) No Lua in stock or Remix data calls the RNG. The Lua build is 4.0-style, so the callable names are the globals `random` and `randomseed`, not `math.random`. The finding's check of official XML for 'math.random' therefore used the wrong pattern. I re-grepped for `random(` and `randomseed(` as bare globals across all official RA3 modding files, and for `random(` in Remix XML. Both returned zero hits. Remix scripts.lua (1786 lines) has zero 'rand' hits. Lua bodies do exist in XML (13785 `<Script` elements, with CurDrawable* calls), so the grep is meaningful.
(2) The sim never draws from CRT rand() each frame. Of the 20 rand() call sites, sub_A702A0 is the Lua function, sub_6BA950 and sub_6BE640 build random digit strings, and the 0x93xxxx–0x99xxxx sites are network code (GameSpy-SDK-like). sub_63CCB0 is the one gameplay-relevant site: a GameInfo reset (it sets "NOMAP") that stores rand() into this+148. In the Zero Hour ancestor this field is m_seed = GetTickCount(), which is set once in the lobby and distributed through setSeed. It is not consumed per frame.
So at vanilla r=2 and under the patch, all players compute the same sim state from this mechanism whatever their fps. What remains is a latent risk for mods, with no link to frame rate. It is not a factor in the 30/60/90 desync. The factual parts are mostly right, apart from the corrections below.

unverified_findings.title: RNG inventory: three separate SAGE streams (logic CB0220 / client CB01F0 / audio CB0208), one generator

summary:
Static analysis only; I built on predecessor transcript agent-a043611affef5deb6 (128 steps) and followed up with about 55 calls of my own. Main result: "source I" comes from one class of bug. The engine does some sim-mutating work once per CLIENT frame, at the top of the client-frame function sub_6027D0, before any phase runs. That work sits in sub_626620 (the engine's vt+148 slot), which the predecessor had already read, and it runs at whatever phase boundary the client frame starts on. Vanilla r=2 groups phases as [1,2,3][4,5,6], so this deferred work always lands after phase 3 or after phase 6. Stall frames (the phase-1 gate fails) do not change that. So vanilla is deterministic across machines with different render rates. With FL_G_RATIO on, the patch schedule for r=4 (60 fps) is [1,2][3][4,5][6], and r=6 (90 fps) is one phase per frame. Three deferred sim paths then move to new phase boundaries:
(M1) GameLogic::processDestroyList, sub_4E2F60. Phase 5 requests it by setting engine+384. sub_619BD0 then runs it at the next client-frame start, which is before phase 6 instead of after it.
(M2) The deferred Object transform-change flush, sub_4D5600 → sub_7C2670 → sub_79E800(...,2). It reacts to moves (partition/shroud/0x4e8 dirty marks and a vt+20 call on the Object+0x328 module, likely contain) and sets the DynamicsUpdate+0x39 flag. With r=4 it also runs before phase 3 and before phase 6.
(M3) The phase gate sub_5FFAD0 (phase == 6/r). With r=4 the schedule's end-of-frame phases are 2, 3, 5, 6, so phase==1 never happens. GhostObjectManager::update (sub_715070, called from GameClient::update) then never runs at 60 fps. At 90 fps it runs between phases 1 and 2 instead of between 3 and 4.
All three disappear with FL_G_RATIO off, because the patch then passes r=2 to its own schedule and gets the vanilla grouping. They also disappear at target 30 fps, which matches the 16886-frame survival. For r=6, M2 also makes the CRC'd PartitionManager and ShroudManager take in moves one logic frame early (phase-1 moves at phase 2, phase-4 moves at phase 5). That explains the live 30-vs-90 fps desync.

The §9.5/§9.6 contradiction goes away. gl+0x50 IS the sim tick: it is incremented at 0x004F82A8 in phase 1. What sets the logic rate is the phase-1 gate (QPC timer sub_615BF0/sub_600F00 in single-player/replay, or network isFrameDataReady), not r. With r=2 at 60 fps the engine runs [1-3][4-6] followed by stall frames. On those stall frames CDB750+196 is 0: the display frame number does not advance, and the deferred work is skipped because its own guards (GL+796, engine+384, display-frame dedupe) stop it. Logic stays at 15 Hz and the sim matches vanilla.

Fix direction: sim-relevant client-frame-start work may run only at the vanilla boundaries (after phase 3 and after phase 6). Either keep r=2 and render extra frames as stall/interpolation frames, or keep RATIO on but gate sub_4D5600, the engine+384 branch of sub_619BD0, and sub_5FFAD0 to those boundaries.

verified.title: processDestroyList runs at the first client-frame start after phase 5; with r=4/6 that is BEFORE phase 6 instead of after it
verified.mechanism: GameLogic::update phase 5 sets engine(CE2F8C)+384 = 1 (line 213098, asm 0x004F8998 `mov byte [ecx+0x180],1`). This flag requests processDestroyList. The request is served only by sub_619BD0, which sub_626620 calls every client frame (sub_626620 is vt+148, called at the top of sub_6027D0 before the phase dispatch). sub_619BD0 reads and clears +384 and, if it was set, calls sub_5F4790, sub_771BF0 (pending-module list CE59C0) and sub_4E2F60(TheGameLogic). sub_4E2F60 is processDestroyList: it removes each pending object's modules from the sleepy buckets GL+220, unlinks it from the object list GL+180 (sub_6DD8C0(this+180,this+184)) and deletes it (obj->vt+28(1)). Vanilla r=2 runs phases 4,5,6 in one client frame, so deletion always happens after phase 6 and before phase 1 of the next frame, including across stall frames. The patched r=4 schedule [1,2][3][4,5][6] (and r=6) sets +384 in the [4,5] frame and deletes at the start of the [6] frame, i.e. BEFORE phase 6. Two consequences: (a) objects destroyed in phases 1-5 are gone (ID lookups return NULL, partition removal, list removal) while phase 6 (bucket 3) runs; in vanilla they are still pending. (b) Objects destroyed during phase 6 of frame N are not deleted until before phase 6 of N+1. They therefore stay in the GL+180 list through N+1 phases 1-5. That list is walked by the GameLogic CRC (sub_4D7F40, which xfers every 10th object in one mode, so an extra entry shifts the sample) and by the phase-1 tail loop sub_78E560(frame). The result is a CRC mismatch whenever a phase-6 destruction precedes a CRC frame. That is a rare event, consistent with the ~2400-frame onset that appears only with RATIO on.

verified.title: Deferred Object transform-change flush runs once per client frame; its phase boundaries move with r
verified.mechanism: Object::setTransform (sub_7ADF20) snapshots the old transform the first time an object moves since the last flush (+484 flag) and appends the object to the double-buffered list dword_CE5930[CE5870]. It then applies only the immediate part, sub_79E800(...,1). The deferred part, sub_79E800(obj,...,oldMtx,oldPos,oldAngle,2), runs in sub_7C2670. Its only caller is sub_4D5600, which runs once per client frame when GL+796 is 0; GL+796 is cleared at the start of every GameLogic::update phase. sub_4D5600's only caller is sub_626620 (client-frame start). If the object moved more than 0.01 or turned, the deferred part: calls Object vt+24 = sub_716C60, which marks the shroud entry dirty (obj+0x9C → grid+76, processed only by ShroudManager::update in phase 5), the obj+0x4E8 entry dirty (owner+8 list) and the PartitionManager entry dirty (obj+0x4E4 → PM+388, processed only by sub_994E50 = PM::update in phase 2); calls vt+20 on the Object+0x328 module or the first entry of vector +0x32C; and sets byte +0x39 of the DynamicsUpdate module (Object+0x390). The +0x328 module is filled from the module's vt+8 interface, which in Generals order is getContain, so the vt+20 call is probably containReactToTransformChange, i.e. it moves passengers. Vanilla flush boundaries are before phase 1 and before phase 4. r=4 adds flushes before phase 3 (moves from phases 1-2: command/script moves and phase-2 collision) and before phase 6 (moves from phases 4-5). Passenger repositioning and DynamicsUpdate flags therefore become visible to phase-3 and phase-6 updates earlier than in vanilla. For r=4 the PM/shroud processing sets are unchanged (see ruled_out). For r=6 (a flush before every phase), PM::update in phase 2 picks up phase-1 moves in the same frame (vanilla: next frame), and ShroudManager::update in phase 5 picks up phase-4 moves in the same frame (vanilla: next frame). PartitionManager (CE2F9C), CollisionManager (CE2FA4) and ShroudManager (CE2FA0) are all xfer'd into the GameLogic CRC, so r=6 should diverge almost immediately. That explains the live 30-vs-90 fps MP desync.

corrections:
1. Remove the DynamicsUpdate part of the sim-risk. The +0x390->+0x39 flag is consumed only in phase 1 by the dynamics manager: GL+404 is built by sub_8E21F0 at dump 212315-212318, its vtable is off_C611F4, and vt+20 = sub_8E4110 reads and clears +57 at dump 1059659-1059662. It is called at dump 212901 inside the `v9 = (a2==1)` block. All schedules flush before phase 1, so the timing of consumption does not change with r. Only the threshold/dedupe artifacts can differ.
2. The claim "for r=4 the PM/shroud processing sets are unchanged" holds only for first-order moves. Objects moved during a flush, for example passengers moved by the contain reaction, go into the other buffer and are only handled at the next boundary. Take a container moved in phase 4 or 5:
   - r=4: the container is flushed before phase 6, its passengers before phase 1, and PM processes them in phase 2 of the next frame.
   - Vanilla: the container is flushed before phase 1 and its passengers before phase 4, so PM processes them one logic frame later.
   This is speculative, because it depends on contained objects still having a PM entry at +0x4E4.
3. Add a second r-dependence: the 0.01 move/angle test and the +484 first-snapshot dedupe apply per flush window. Finer windows can suppress reactions or add extra ones compared with vanilla.
4. Keep the r=6 PM and shroud claims (phase-1 moves reach PM in phase 2, phase-4 moves reach the shroud in phase 5, both in the same frame). The code supports them, but it is not shown that they diverge the sim or the CRC. Label "explains the live 30-vs-90 MP desync" as speculative.
5. The fix logic checks out. At sub_626620 entry, this[22] holds the last completed phase: in vanilla that is always 3 or 6; under r=4 it is 6, 2, 3 or 5; under r=6 it is 1 to 6. Letting the flush run only when this[22] is 3 or 6 therefore reproduces the vanilla windows. One side effect: mode 2 also clears bits (&=0xF9) in byte 319 of the object behind a1+244 (possibly the Drawable, speculative). Deferring the flush also delays that clear on client-side frames.

1. The CRC claim is partly wrong. PartitionManager (CE2F9C) and CollisionManager (CE2FA4) add only a constant to the CRC. Their snapshot vtables are PM+0x24 = C6AF88 and CM = C6B02C, and the xferSnapshot target in slot 3 is 0x6EA320, which only xfers two constant version bytes. Only ShroudManager adds real state: 0x9938B0 → sub_993470 hashes a rolling 1/20 of the shroud cells per CRC, chosen by GL frame%20, 40 bytes per cell. A PM timing difference is therefore not caught by the CRC directly. It only shows up once changed range-query results alter object state.

2. "r=6 diverges almost immediately" is overstated. In the Generals ancestor, AIUpdate is PHASE_INITIAL (AIUpdate.h:586) and position integration is PhysicsUpdate PHASE_PHYSICS (PhysicsUpdate.h:212). That probably maps to list 0 (phases 3-4) and list 1 (phase 5), but the mapping is speculative. At r=6, phase-5 moves are flushed before phase 6 and reach PM (next phase 2) and Shroud (next phase 5) at exactly the vanilla points. The r=6 shroud difference needs a position change in phase 4 (the last 20% of list 0). The r=6 PM difference needs a move in phase 1 (commands, scripts, object creation). Both are plausible but unverified.

3. The finding left out one r=4 effect. Mode 2 always clears bits 1-2 of byte +319 on the object at +244, even when the object did not move. It also left out a window-split effect: the 0.01 move/turn threshold is measured against a snapshot that resets at every flush. Splitting a window can change whether vt+24 fires. This is rare, e.g. moves that cancel out, or small moves that only pass the threshold when added together.

4. Extra detail: the vanilla flush before phase 4 falls inside list-0 processing (phase 3 runs the first 80% of list 0, phase 4 the rest).

5. The fix (only allow the 0x6266F7 flush when this[22] is 3 or 6 at client-frame start) is consistent with vanilla. It should also allow the initial or post-reset state, and stall frames are harmless because the GL+796 guard stays in place. summary:
This was a static-only pass (dump G:\IDA\RA3_1.12.game.c plus the binary). Nothing was run and no files were changed.

(1) In vanilla, r is fixed at 2 on every machine. Each logic frame always takes exactly two calls to the client-frame loop sub_6027D0 (phases 1-3, then 4-6, run by sub_616130). No code path runs more than one logic frame per client frame. The lockstep gate sits at phase 1 only: if the network frame data is not ready, the client frame advances nothing. A slow machine therefore slows the whole game; it does not run fewer client frames per logic frame.

What does differ between vanilla machines is how often GameClient::update and the draw run. sub_626620 skips GameClient::update (CDB750 vtbl+20) through sub_602720 on machines that cannot hold 30 fps, and when catching up after a stall. So such a machine runs it 1 time per logic frame, a fast one 2 times.

But the display-frame counter is incremented at the top of sub_626620, before that skip. So on every vanilla machine it advances exactly 2 per logic frame. The game clock follows it (clock += frame delta × 33), and so does all per-client-frame work done before the skip.

So the HANDOFF §22.3 premise is only half true. Vanilla tolerates different render/GameClient-update counts, but it never had machines with different display-frame counts, clock advance or client-frame counts. Any hidden dependence of the simulation on those quantities was undetectable in vanilla and would break exactly when r differs. That fits every measurement so far.

(2) RA3 has no Generals-style exchange of frame rate or run-ahead. The only timing message is MSG_ANNOUNCE_RTT (567). It carries round-trip times plus one per-player byte and is applied, in lockstep, to the network table only. Run-ahead is a local, sender-side value in [2,15], set from RTT and wall clock. It only decides which frame the sender stamps its commands for, so it cannot change the simulation. Local pacing (sub_6293D0, flt_CAFF7C, this[95]) is local and wall-clock only. No transmitted or lockstep-applied value is derived from CAF9D4, CDBC50/54/5C/D34, the display frame number or the clock.

(3) Desync is detected by MSG_LOGIC_CRC (545). It is sent at phase 1 when frame % interval == 0; the multiplayer interval is *(CE3A74+36), falling back to 150. The CRC covers: the logic object list, the logic RNG only (0xCB0220; the client RNG at 0xCB01F0 and the audio RNG at 0xCB0208 are excluded), partition/collision/shroud-style subsystems, the player list, AI, script engine (CDD190), CE1B18, CD8CCC and per-player sums. No client-side state is included. The engine also has built-in diagnostics: -verifyClientCRC (byte_CE2F5A) and -deepCRC (byte_CE2F5B, a per-frame CRC dump). Using them is the most direct way to find the first field that diverges.

(a) The clock CE1388, and with it CF1B0C and D075CC, advances only inside GameClient::update → TheDisplay vtbl+48 = sub_5FE9D0. (b) The pre-skip calls in sub_626620 run on every sub_6027D0 call, including network-stall retries and paused iterations. Their count per logic frame varies between machines in vanilla too. Only the frame bump is +196-gated.

refutations:
I re-read every cited site. One of the finding's three headline claims holds. The other two misread the code.

HOLDS: the display-frame counter. GameEngine vtbl base is 0xC0D5B8. sub_6027D0 is at +0x14, sub_616130 at +0x90, sub_626620 at +0x94, sub_6293D0 at +0x38. sub_6027D0 calls vtbl+148 (sub_626620) first in every call. sub_626620 bumps GameClient+0x48 only when CDB750+196 is set. setFrame is vtbl+56 = sub_53FB00 (`mov [ecx+0x48],eax`) and getFrame is vtbl+116 = sub_8B1130. The pseudocode shows no other vtbl+56 caller and no direct access to CDB750+72. The field is zeroed in sub_53CC20. sub_616130 batches phases 3 at a time for r=2, so each logic frame takes 2 successful calls: one entered at this[22]==6 or >6, one entered at 3. Stall retries clear +196, so they do not bump. The result is exactly r bumps per logic frame. sub_602720/sub_5FFAD0 cannot skip on the mid call (this[22]==3). So GameClient::update (sub_542DF0) runs 1 or 2 times per machine on the non-stall calls, plus possibly more during stall retries.

MISREAD 1: the clock. The only writer of CE1388 is sub_5FE9D0; sub_5F4310 only resets it to 0. sub_5FE9D0 is TheDisplay (CDB71C, primary vtbl 0xC0B040) vtbl+48. It is called only from inside GameClient::update, near the end of sub_542DF0. GameClient::update is the skippable part of sub_626620, and sub_626620 runs BEFORE the same sub_6027D0 call dispatches sub_616130(1), which runs GameLogic phases 1-3. sub_4F81F0 does `++*(v2+80)` and the rest of the phase-1 work there. Compare the two machines on the call entered at this[22]==6:
- Non-skipping machine: sub_5FE9D0 has already added (F_C - F_B)*33, so logic phases 1-3 read CE1388 = 33*F_C.
- Skipping machine (this[95]<=1): logic phases 1-3 read 33*F_B, a 33 ms lag. The same applies to WW3D time CF1B0C (sub_936910) and APT time D075CC (sub_99BF90).
The 'catch-up' through (displayFrame - CAFDDC)*33 only happens at the next draw, which is the mid call before phases 4-6. It also exists only in the draw branch. The other branch (v6 = CE2FA8+80 or sub_557260) does `CE1388 += CE176C`, one unit per call, and still sets CAFDDC. There, skipped frames are lost for good. So the claim 'any sim read of the clock was lockstep-deterministic in vanilla and could never desync' is false for reads in phases 1-3.

MISREAD 2: the pre-skip work. sub_6027D0 calls vtbl+148 before the sub_557220 pause check and on every stall retry. Stall retries are main-loop iterations of sub_6293D0 in which sub_616130(1) sets +196=0 and this[22] is restored to 7, 8, 9... Only the frame bump is gated by +196. The other pre-skip calls are not gated: sub_99F970, CDB71C+268, sub_6FDC60, CEBD54+20, sub_619BD0, sub_6D1B70(CE3F04), sub_4D5600 and CD6C9C+156 (whose argument this[22]+10*frame changes on each retry). They run once per sub_6027D0 call, not exactly 2 times per logic frame, and stall counts differ between machines. Most of them look like queue-drain or one-shot routines: sub_4D5600 is a one-shot latch and sub_6FDC60 drains a list. So this is probably harmless, but the claim as stated is wrong.

MINOR: this[95] has hysteresis (`|v19-10*this[95]|>8`). From 2 it drops to 1 only when the clamped 64-frame average is 17 fps or less (v19<=11). From 1 it returns to 2 only at 30 fps. It is not simply '1 under 30 fps'. The clamp to [15,30] happens only when CE3A8C is set; otherwise v13=30.

This is a partial refutation. The display-frame-counter part of F2 holds. Two of its three "always 2 per logic frame" claims do not, and the claimed critical sim-risk has no demonstrated path into simulation.

What holds:
- GameEngine vtable base 0xC0D5B8. Slot +0x14 is sub_6027D0 (0xC0D5CC), +0x90 is sub_616130 (0xC0D648) and +0x94 is sub_626620 (0xC0D64C).
- sub_6027D0 calls vtbl+148 (sub_626620) first. It sets CDB750+196 after that call and dispatches the logic phases (vtbl+144) after that.
- In sub_626620, the display-frame bump (`setFrame(getFrame()+1)`, dump lines 464728-464733) comes before the skip test sub_602720 (line 464776).
- The frame is GameClient[18] (+72). getFrame is sub_8B1130, setFrame is sub_53FB00 (vtbl+56), and GameClient::reset sub_53CC20 (vtbl+16) zeroes it. The only setFrame call through CDB750 in the dump is at line 464732.
- The bump is gated by CDB750+196. sub_616130 clears that flag on a phase-1 network stall (LABEL_29) and sub_6027D0 clears it on pause, so the counter rises exactly once per successful client-frame advance. That is 2 per logic frame in vanilla, whether or not the frame was skipped. This part is confirmed and matters.
- The sub_602720, sub_5FFAD0 and sub_6293D0 quotes are accurate.
- The draw sub_5FE9D0 is slot +0x30 of the vtable at off_C0B040, which belongs to the CDB71C display object. sub_542DF0 calls it as CDB71C vtbl+48 (around line 279867), so a skip also skips the draw and the clock bump. The later catch-up by `(frame - CAFDDC) * 33` is correct.

What fails under the cadence lens:
(1) Pre-skip work is not "exactly 2 per logic frame on every machine".
- The main loop sub_6293D0 calls vtbl+20 (sub_6027D0) every iteration, and sub_6027D0 calls sub_626620 unconditionally, before both the pause check and the phase dispatch.
- On a network stall, sub_616130(a2=1) takes LABEL_29 and sub_6027D0 puts this[22] back to 7. sub_626620 keeps running every iteration, and sub_602720's `this[22] > 6` branch exists only for this state.
- So sub_6FDC60, sub_6D1B70(CE3F04), CEBD54+20, sub_619BD0, sub_4D5600 and CD6C9C+156 run 2 + (stall/pause iterations) times per logic frame. That count differs between machines in vanilla multiplayer.
- They look like queue drains or one-shots, so the count probably does not matter. Either way the claim is wrong, and vanilla already tolerates their count varying.
- GameClient::update also runs on stall iterations (the not-ready branch returns 0). Only the drawable loop is gated by `CAF900 == frame`. The managers after it and the draw run on every call.

(2) The clock is not lockstep at the moment logic reads it.
- A skip can happen only when this[22] == 6, which is the iteration that then runs phases 1..3. At the mid phase sub_5FFAD0 is true, so that iteration is never skipped.
- On a skipping machine, CE1388, CF1B0C and D075CC are therefore 33 ms behind during logic phases 1..3 and catch up only in the phase 4..6 iteration.
- So a sim read of the clock in phases 1..3 would differ between vanilla machines with this[95]=1 and this[95]=2. "Any sim read of the clock was lockstep-deterministic" is false. Only the per-logic-frame total (66 ms) and reads in phases 4..6 match.

(3) The this[95] claim is overstated.
- There is hysteresis. It drops from 2 to 1 only when v19 <= 11, i.e. an average of 17 fps or less. It returns to 2 only at exactly 30 fps (v19 = 20).
- The "fps" is measured over main-loop iterations (dword_CE2F80), stall iterations included. So a machine running at 20-29 fps with this[95]=2 stays at 2 and does not skip.

(4) Reachability to simulation is not shown.
- F2 names no reader of CDB750 vtbl+116 or CE1388 inside GameLogic or the CRC path.
- The direct instruction readers of CE1388 are only sub_5F4310 (writer), sub_5FE9D0, and sub_90C1B0, sub_90ECF0, sub_90F820, sub_90FCE0, sub_90FD20, sub_90FD90, sub_90FF70 and sub_911A40.
- sub_90FCE0/90FD20/90FD90 open with a `dword_CE1388 == this[45]` time-cache compare, which looks like W3D render caching. Whether any of these reach the sim is speculative.
- "Confirmed" and "critical" for a sim-risk are not supported. This is a scoping hypothesis.

(5) "Explains why any change of r desyncs" does not cover source II.
- Source II appears regardless of FL_G_RATIO, i.e. with r = 2, where the display-frame cadence is unchanged. So the counter cannot explain it.
- The clock redirect with r = 2 (clock step g_msPerFrame at 60 fps, about half the vanilla advance per logic frame) is a candidate. That is speculative.

verified.title: Client-originated notification commands (camera/audio/EVA/scroll) carry patch-affected timing, but they travel in the lockstep stream
verified.mechanism: The client builds commands whose value or timing comes from client behaviour, and the patch changes that behaviour (FL_G_CAMERA, scroll normalization): 550 MSG_CHANGE_CAMERA_ARRIVED_AT_WAYPOINTID (sub_5B9B90, sub_5EA820), 576 MSG_SET_SCRIPT_FLAG_ON_COMPLETION (sub_518E00), 583 MSG_NOTIFY_CAMERA_RESET (sub_5ECF00), and 572-582 audio/EVA/camera movement/rotation/zoom/scroll-distance/trigger-area (sub_91D0B0..sub_91E3F0). They are appended to the command stream and dispatched in sub_4F23E0 on every machine at the stamped frame, so they cannot desync multiplayer. They can change script outcomes relative to a vanilla run, mainly in campaign scripts. For replays, the recorded copies are the ones that execute.
evidence: case 550 @~210086: `if (sub_838F60(*(a3+16))) sub_4EEC70(*arg0);` (executed for any player, not only the local one)
verified.fix_proposal: No change for multiplayer. Check whether these notifications are also generated locally during replay playback (see open questions).
corrections:
1. sub_5EA820 is the View constructor. It sets *this = off_C0B2E8, and its 550(0) is sent once at construction, only when the +9744 field is non-zero. It is not timing-driven and should not be a fix site. The timing-driven 550 comes from sub_5B9B90 (View vtbl+0x64), which sub_5C4070 and sub_5C3A20 call once per display frame.
2. The sub_91D0B0..sub_91E3F0 range sends 581 (sub_91D0B0), 579 (sub_91D0F0), 580 (sub_91D170), 574 (sub_91D320), 572 (sub_91D390), 573 (sub_91DFF0) and 582 (sub_91E3F0). It is not a continuous 572-582. 575 is MSG_ACTIVATE_RED_ALERT, 577 is MSG_SET_FLAG_ON_VIDEO_COMPLETION and 578 is MSG_NOTIFY_CAMERA_MOVEMENT_UPDATED; none of them is emitted there.
3. Wording: FL_G_CAMERA and FL_G_SCROLL do not introduce the timing change. The higher render rate speeds up per-display-frame camera and scroll stepping. FL_G_CAMERA and FL_G_SCROLL (both off by default) restore vanilla per-second speed.
4. Only some messages have render-rate-dependent timing: 550, 579/580/581 and possibly 583. 572-574 (audio/EVA status) have no shown link to render rate (speculative).
5. Case 550 handler: the full form is ThePlayerList(dword_CE8C9C)->getNth(msg.player) != 0 ⇒ dword_CDD178->map(+0x38)[arg0] = 2. The finding's short form omitted the ECX objects.
6. The finding's open question can be answered: during playback, sub_624670 → sub_608BA0 removes the locally generated network-range messages (except 545), so only the recorded copies execute.

- Scope of the 572–582 range: the sub_91Dxxx family creates only 572 (sub_91D390), 573 (sub_91DFF0), 574 (sub_91D320), 579 (sub_91D0F0), 580 (sub_91D170), 581 (sub_91D0B0) and 582 (sub_91E3F0). Nothing there creates 575, 577 or 578. The dispatcher sub_4F23E0 has no case for 577 or 578, and 575 (sub_84D9F0 on the sender's player object) was not traced to a creator here.
- The replay open question is resolved, not still open: Recorder::updatePlayback sub_624670 calls cullBadCommands sub_608BA0 first. That deletes the network-range copies the client generates locally, so only the recorded copies run.
- The finding contradicts an existing comment in src/framelab.cpp at the FL_G_CAMERA definition (about lines 829–830). That comment says co-op campaign players with different FL_G_CAMERA settings are bound to desync earlier. For these notification paths that is wrong, because the notifications are lockstep commands. The comment could still hold for other paths, such as a script condition that polls the tactical view (camera) directly from the logic side. That was not examined here.
- Two small parts of the "handlers read no local state" check were not read. The 574 else-branch of sub_58CF00 (after dump line 336120) was not read. The object that sub_4EEC70 and sub_596B90 insert into is not visible in the pseudocode (ECX dropped); only the value 2 is inserted, and the key is the message argument.

The mechanism and conclusion are correct; only the classification is wrong. Record this as a ruled_out item (MP-safe path), not as a sim-risk. It should include the evidence the finding lacked:
(a) the network send path in sub_6665B0: range 501–1298, all-slot mask 63, with a local-only mask only when msg byte +112 is set, which these generators never set;
(b) propagation sub_607B00 → TheCommandList dword_CE2FBC;
(c) the replay cull sub_608BA0 called from sub_624670, which answers the finding's open question: local copies are generated during playback but deleted before execution.

Minor fixes:
- Case 550 calls sub_4EEC70 with ECX = dword_CDD178 (Hex-Rays drops it). 579/580/581/583 write fields of dword_CDD178. 576 calls sub_595700 on dword_CDD190.
- Types 577 and 578 have no case in sub_4F23E0 (the case list jumps 576 → 579), so the "572–582" span should not be read as a contiguous set of handled types.
- In MP each client sends its own copies (for example each player's 581 overwrites CDD178+0x2C in turn). That is deterministic but last-writer-wins, and it only matters for map scripts.
- Fix sites 0x005EA820 and 0x0091D0B0 need no change for MP.
refutations:
I checked this through the counterfactual lens. The finding's facts hold, and they show there is no cross-machine risk. With the lens rule applied, the "sim-risk" classification is refuted: every player computes the same sim state at 30, 60 or 90 fps. The item belongs in ruled_out, not among the risks.

1) Every generator appends to TheMessageStream (dword_CE2FB8), and none of them sets the local-only flag.
- refs.py shows `mov ecx,[0xCE2FB8]` before the sub_60C4A0 call in all four functions: sub_518E00 @0x005192BD, sub_5B9B90 @0x005B9BA0, sub_5EA820 @0x005EAC6A and sub_5ECF00 @0x005ECF86.
- The 0x91Dxxx generators pass dword_CE2FB8 explicitly (dump 1106858 onward).
- sub_60C4A0 (dump 442235) stamps player index = localPlayer+40+32 and clears msg byte +112.

2) The stream drains into TheCommandList. sub_607B00(dword_CE2FB8) runs the translators and then calls `sub_600500(dword_CE2FBC, this[9])` (dump 438201; callers at 204933, 279702, 464785).

3) The network layer sends every message in this range to all players. sub_6665B0 (dump 518942) is RA3's Network::GetCommandsFromCommandList.
- Messages with `v4 > 500 && v4 < 1299` are wrapped in a net command and sent with `sub_662A80(this[10], msg, 63, cmd)`, then removed from TheCommandList.
- 63 is the all-slots mask. The mask shrinks to 1<<localId only when `sub_A81320(msg)` is true, i.e. msg byte +112 is set.
- None of the 550/572–583 generators set +112. The only Hex-Rays write of 1 to msg+112 is in the unrelated sub_7623B0 (dump 731348).
- Types 550 and 572–583 all fall in the range 501–1298, so they are lockstep commands executed on every machine at the same frame.

4) The handlers don't depend on which machine runs them. In the disassembly of sub_4F23E0:
- 550 → `mov ecx,[0xCDD178]; call sub_4EEC70` @0x004F2D2E.
- 579/580/581 write floats to [CDD178+0x30/+0x34/+0x2C] @0x004F2CC4..0x004F2D02.
- 582 → `call sub_596B90` with ecx=[CDD178] @0x004F2D61.
- 583 writes a byte to [CDD178+0x74] @0x004F2D94.
- 576 → `call sub_595700` with ecx=[0xCDD190] @0x004F2C5F.
- Each handler is gated only by `sub_838F60(msg+16)` on the PlayerList. Nothing depends on the local player.

Result: at vanilla fixed r=2 this is deterministic across machines. With mixed 30/60/90 fps, each client's own copies (with its own fps-dependent timing and values) reach every peer and execute at the same stamped frame, so all peers stay identical. The fps only changes when and what a client decides to send, in the same way that human input timing does. That is not a divergence.

5) Replays: the recorder playback update sub_624670 calls sub_608BA0 first (dump 463179). This is cullBadCommands: it deletes TheCommandList messages with `v2 > 500 && v2 < 1299 && v2 != 545` (dump 439110). Locally generated notifications are thrown away during playback, and only the recorded copies execute. Recording keeps the same range (sub_624F40, dump 463593). This settles the finding's open question, and these commands cannot explain "source I/II" replay desyncs.

What is left is a single-machine difference from a vanilla run: script timing in campaign or skirmish without a network, where TheCommandList is processed locally. That is not a multiplayer determinism risk.

unverified_findings.title: Vanilla r is structurally fixed at 2 on every machine; no catch-up path runs >1 logic frame per client frame
unverified_findings.mechanism: GameEngine vtable base 0xC0D5B8: +0x14 = sub_6027D0 (update, @0xC0D5CC), +0x90 = sub_616130 (phase batch, @0xC0D648), +0x94 = sub_626620 (per-client-frame engine/client work, @0xC0D64C). Each call to sub_6027D0 first calls vtbl+148 (sub_626620), then advances phase this[22] and dispatches vtbl+144 (sub_616130). sub_616130 computes r = CAF9D4/CAF9D0 = 2. For a2=1: result = 6*((2*0)/6+1)/2 = 3, so it runs phases 1,2,3. For a2=4: result = 6, so it runs 4,5,6. The loop never crosses into the next logic frame. The only network gate is at phase 1: if CE3A8C vtbl+56 (frame data ready) is false, or CD8CE4+348 is set, it goes to LABEL_29 and sets *(CDB750+196)=0. sub_6027D0 then restores this[22] (=7, meaning a stall), so logic does not advance on that client frame. The main loop sub_6293D0 calls update() exactly once per iteration. So a slow vanilla machine produces fewer logic frames per second: the whole game slows through lockstep plus local pacing, and r stays 2. The fast-forward branch in sub_5FE9D0 (draw only when display frame % 30 == 0) applies only when the replay-FF flag CE2FA8+80 or the debugger RunAppFast is set. It skips drawing only and leaves the phase cadence unchanged.

unverified_findings.title: No frame-rate or run-ahead negotiation; MSG_ANNOUNCE_RTT and run-ahead do not depend on any patched value and cannot change the simulation
unverified_findings.mechanism: The message-name table sub_606B70 (ids 501-595) has no run-ahead or frame-rate message, and the binary has no RunAhead/FrameRate/FrameMetrics strings. summary:
Static pass on generic client-to-simulation data channels, about 65 tool calls. No earlier transcript existed for this dimension. I reused scratchpad cg2.pkl (direct-call graph) and the finished results of the sibling agents (logic-rng a38872cd631f152d9, phase-scheduler a4c4f9d03273366e5).

Bottom line: I found no generic channel that explains the skirmish desync. The strong candidate is still the phase-scheduler agent's deferred per-client-frame work in sub_626620 (M1/M2/M3).

Channels found, by item:
(1) Display frame number. It has 100 textual reads in 84 functions. It is incremented once per client frame in sub_626620, the same function that hosts the deferred sim work. Every other reader is a client consumer (draw, UI, particles, audio, LaserUpdate), including the four readers whose addresses sit in the logic range.
(2) Wall clock. timeGetTime, GetTickCount and QueryPerformanceCounter have zero readers in the GameLogic range (0x4D0000-0x4FFFFF) or the object-module range (0x690000-0x8D0000). The QPC reads in sub_600E90/600F00 are the phase-1 timer gate (another dimension). dword_CE1388, dword_CF1B0C and dword_D075CC are read only by the main tick, W3D draw modules, particles and shaders.
(3) View state, confirmed. GameLogic::update phase 1 (sub_4F81F0) freezes the sim on `view->vt156() && !view->vt108()`. This is the Generals `isTimeFrozen() && !isCameraMovementFinished()` idiom. The camera advances per display frame in sub_5EB5E0. The scheduler keeps calling phases 2-6 during the freeze. The camera script conditions (CAMERA_MOVEMENT_FINISHED etc.) exist, but I did not find their RA3 evaluator. Both only matter on maps whose scripts freeze time or test the camera (campaign / co-op), not in normal skirmish.
(4) Drawable state. Logic bone queries go through sub_51E180 = Drawable::getPristineBonePositions. It is keyed on the model-condition flags, not the animation, so it is deterministic. Two weaker leads remain:
- The LaserUpdate path: logic sub_7563F0 destroys the laser object when its drawable has no LaserUpdate module, and the client module destroys its drawable after a lifetime counted in display frames.
- W3DScriptedModelDraw creates bodies in the logic-owned physics world. That world steps at logic rate with dt = 1/15 from dword_CAF9D0.
(5) RNG. The logic RNG agent already established three separate streams and a clean Lua state split. Audio throttling uses timeGetTime plus the audio RNG and stays client-only.

Vanilla premise: every channel found here counts in display frames. Each is identical across vanilla machines because r is fixed at 2 (6 phases per 2 client frames). They split only when r becomes 4 or 6, or when patch groups such as FL_G_CAMERA or FL_G_DERIVED2 change the display-frame length of a client timer. That supports the corrected HANDOFF §22 reading.

1) Freeze initiator: script action 0x16 calls view vt+120 = sub_5EACA0 (+9749=1) at dump 357202. Actions 0x71/0x8B go through sub_555F90 to vt+340 = sub_5D3ED0, which stops camera movement: it zeroes +9620, +1048, +1088, +1124, +1208 and +9740, so it ends a freeze rather than starting one.

2) Cadence: a frozen phase 1 leaves CDB750+0xC4 = 0, and sub_6027D0 then puts phase 7 back (0x602921 `mov [esi+58h],edi`). So phase 1 is retried on every display frame. The only other phases that run during the freeze are those batched in the same call as phase 1:
   - vanilla r=2: phases 2 and 3 once per display frame
   - r=4: phase 2 once per display frame
   - r=6: nothing, because the `r<6` batch is skipped

   - vanilla: D×phase2 + D×phase3
   - 60 fps: about D'×phase2 (D' = D, or about 2D with FL_G_CAMERA on), no phase 3
   - 90 fps: no phase 2 or 3
   The formula "display frames / r" is wrong.

   - Skipping phases 2..6 after a frozen phase 1 diverges from vanilla, which does run 2 and 3.
   - Making FL_G_CAMERA mandatory does not help: at 90 fps it triples the phase-1 retries and still leaves phase 2/3 at zero.

With FL_G_CAMERA on, that means firing on each display frame where accumulated camera ms crosses a 33 ms boundary. Without FL_G_CAMERA, it means once per display frame, but the batch must be forced even when r >= 6.

4) The sim impact is still speculative. Phase 2 is Partition/Collision/ShieldSphere manager updates, and repeating them at a frozen frame number is the main suspect. Phase 3 repeats are mostly idempotent because of the wake scheduling.

The freeze gate itself is read correctly. In sub_4F81F0, when a2==1 the code calls vt+0x9C and vt+0x6C with ECX=[0xCDB7B4] (disasm 0x4F824A-0x4F826D). In the view's primary vtable at 0xC0B2E8, vt+156 is sub_5EACB0, which returns byte this[9749] (isTimeFrozen). vt+108 is sub_5B9840, which returns true when no camera movement is active (isCameraMovementFinished). A frozen phase 1 with no type-1 message pending sets CDB750+196=0 and exits through LABEL_141 without ++GL+80.

Three central claims do not hold.

(1) Scheduling model is wrong. The finding ignores what sub_6027D0 does after the dispatch (dump 433886; disasm 0x602908-0x602924). After it calls vt+0x90 (= sub_616130) with phase 1, it tests [CDB750+0xC4]. If that byte is 0, it restores [esi+0x58] to the saved counter (>=7), so phase 1 is retried on the very next client frame. The phase counter never walks 2..6 while frozen. The only other phases that run are the ones the batch inside sub_616130 dispatches in the same call as phase 1:
- Vanilla r=2: disasm 0x61626E-0x6162B5 gives loop bound 4, so phases 2 and 3 run.
- Patched r=4: P2 fl_hook_batch(1,4) returns target 2, so phase 2 only.
- Patched r=6: `cmp edi,6; jge 0x616330` at 0x616265 skips the batch, so no phase at all.
Phases 4-6 are never dispatched during a freeze in any configuration. So "phases 2-6 keep being scheduled" is false, and "freeze length in phase dispatches = display frames / r" is also false: vanilla dispatches phase 2 and phase 3 once per display frame, which is not divided by r.

(2) Freeze trigger misattributed. Script actions 0x71/0x8B call sub_555F90, which calls view vt+340 = sub_5D3ED0 (vtable slot 0xC0B43C). That function zeroes the camera-movement state (this+9620, 1048, 1088, 1124, 1208, 1209, 9740, ...). It stops or finishes camera movement; it does not start a freeze. The freeze is set by action 0x16 (sub_5A2B40, dump 357202), which calls view vt+120 = sub_5EACA0 (slot 0xC0B360), which sets this[9749]=1.

(3) Consequently the differential and the fix are wrong. "With FL_G_CAMERA on the count is about the same as vanilla" is false. Even with the camera timing matched, 90 fps dispatches zero phase-2/3 calls per frozen display frame versus two in vanilla, and 60 fps dispatches one (phase 2 only). Making FL_G_CAMERA mandatory would not make the machines agree.

A residual risk remains in corrected form (see corrections). Its sim impact is still unverified.

verified.title: FL_G_ANIMGATE (P7) desyncs because it gates the phase executor, not a draw update
verified.mechanism: P7 rewrites the 13-byte call at 0x00602942 in sub_6027D0 (`mov edx,[esi]; push eax; mov eax,[edx+0x90]; mov ecx,esi; call eax`) into `push eax; push esi; call fl_hook_frameupdate`. The hook forwards only when (phase-1)%3==0. Slot +0x90 of the GameEngine vtable (base 0xC0D5B8, slot address 0xC0D648) is sub_616130. sub_616130 runs the phase: it holds the phase-1 network gate and calls GameLogic vt+52 = sub_4F81F0(a2). At r=6 the engine's catch-up/batch loop, which sits inside `if (r<6)`, is skipped, so each client frame runs exactly one phase. P7 therefore drops phases 2, 3, 5 and 6 of every logic frame: PartitionManager/Collision (phase 2), sleepy buckets (3-6), ShroudManager (5). The simulation diverges at once. verified.mechanism: fl_hook_batch returns fl_target_phase(phase, r) + 1. At r=2 this gives targets 3 (a2=1) and 6 (a2=4), matching vanilla's 6*((r*(a2-1))/6+1)/r. So with FL_G_RATIO off (r=2 passed in), P2 is bit-identical to vanilla. At r=4 (RATIO on) the schedule is phases_done = 2,3,5,6, i.e. client frames [1,2][3][4,5][6]. sub_626620 (vt+0x94) runs at the start of every client frame, before the phase dispatch, and does sim-mutating work: processDestroyList (sub_619BD0 → sub_4E2F60 when engine+384 is set in phase 5), the deferred transform-change flush (sub_4D5600 → sub_7C2670 → sub_79E800(...,2)), and the ghost update gated by sub_5FFAD0 (phase == 6/r). That work now runs between phases 2|3 and 5|6 instead of only after 3 and after 6. These are sibling findings M1-M3. P2 is the code that creates the r=4 grouping. At r=6 P2 never runs, because the block is inside `if (r<6)`, but the engine's own one-phase-per-frame schedule has the same problem. The risk therefore belongs to r>2 as a whole, not to the P2 bytes.

corrections:
1) The sub_5FFAD0 gate does not behave as stated. With R1 on, 0x5FFAD0 computes 6/r: 3 at r=2, 1 at r=4, and 1 at r=6 via the r>=6 branch. sub_626620 reaches the gate before the phase dispatch, through sub_602720 (0x626732) and through sub_542DF0 (dump 279744, which gates sub_715070(dword_CE5888)).
- In vanilla it is true once per logic frame, after phase 3 (this[22]==3), not after phase 6.
- Under P2 at r=4, this[22] at frame start is only ever 6, 2, 3 or 5, so the gate never fires.
- At r=6 it fires after phase 1.
So at r=4, P2 suppresses this work completely rather than moving it. The same applies to the network pacing branch in sub_602720 and to sub_6293D0 (dump 466731), which adjusts flt_CAFF7C. Calling the ghost update sim-mutating is speculative.

2) Sharper evidence for M1: sub_4E2F60 is not just a generic processDestroyList. It swap-removes update-module entries from the GameLogic buckets at +220+16*k. Phases 3-6 iterate those same buckets in sub_4F81F0 (phase 6 walks bucket 3, and it also swap-removes entries itself). Running sub_4E2F60 before phase 6 instead of after it therefore changes the membership and order of what phase 6 iterates.

3) M2 detail: GameLogic+796 is cleared at the entry of every phase (0x4F8232). The number of flushes per logic frame goes from 2 (vanilla) to 4 (r=4) to 6 (r=6), and each flush also toggles the double buffer dword_CE5870.

4) Minor: after P2, eax is target+1 instead of target when the loop does not run. The return value of vtbl+0x90 is discarded by sub_6027D0, so this is harmless.

For the fix proposal: latching sub_5FFAD0 only at the vanilla boundaries is not enough. At r=4 it needs a phase test that can actually be satisfied at frame start under the P2 schedule. For example, "a boundary crossed phase 3", or this[22] in {3} instead of == 6/r.

1. The destroy-list processing is MOVED, not added. The runs between phases 2|3 and after phase 6 at r=4 find engine+384 already clear. At r=4 and r=6, sub_4E2F60 runs ONLY between phases 5 and 6. This has two effects, and the second is stronger than the finding states:
   (a) Phase 6 (bucket 3 updates) iterates buckets that were already swap-removed, so the update order of surviving modules differs.
   (b) Objects marked destroyed during phase 6 of logic frame N stay in the object list, partition and buckets through phases 1-5 of frame N+1. That includes the phase-1 CRC point, sub_4F1D80 → sub_4D7F40 plus message 545 (dump ~212855). Whether sub_4D7F40 hashes destroyed-but-not-removed objects is speculative.
2. sub_5FFAD0 (M3, 'ghost update') should come out of the simulation fix_sites. Its callers are sub_542DF0 (dump 279744: drawable fog/ghost loop and sub_715070 render-object cleanup), sub_602720 (client-update skip), sub_6293D0 (dump 466731: net pacing flt_CAFF7C) and sub_70F350 (dump 663116: interpolation). That is a likely visual or leak bug (ghost cleanup never runs at 60 fps), not a desync.
3. Fix detail: GL+796 is cleared at the entry of every phase in sub_4F81F0, so it cannot serve as the boundary latch. Gate on the engine phase instead: run sub_4D5600 only when this[22] ∈ {3,6}, and consume engine+384 in sub_619BD0 only when this[22]==6. Both hold at r=2, 4 and 6, because phases 3 and 6 always end a client frame in fl_phases_done.
4. Not checked (open): the rest of sub_626620 also runs per client frame with GL+161=1: sub_6FDC60, dword_CEBD54 vt+20, sub_62B190/sub_6783D0, and sub_8FD680(dword_CE9C38) inside sub_619BD0. Any of these could be further simulation reach at r>2.

(a) The sub_4D5600 latch GL+796 is cleared at the start of every phase call (sub_4F81F0 around dump 212755, `*(_BYTE*)(v2+796)=0`). So sub_7C2670 fires on every client frame: before phases 1 and 4 at r=2, and before phases 1, 3, 4 and 6 at r=4. The 'finding' calls it a transform flush with sim effect, but its path is sub_79E800(...,a6=2), which takes only the bit-2 branch. That branch clears the bits at +244->+319 (mask 0xF9), and on a >0.01 change calls obj vt+24 plus the +808/+812 vt+20 notify. The bit-1 branch, which does the partition/NaN update via sub_78E670 and sub_4EE150, is not taken. Whether this path is sim-visible is speculative.

(b) sub_5FFAD0 is not called directly by sub_626620. Its callers are sub_602720 (the net-lag frame-skip check with flt_CAFF7C, called from sub_626620), sub_542DF0 at dump 279744 (gates sub_715070(dword_CE5888)), sub_6293D0 and sub_70F350. It is an R1 site (kSigFpsGlobals, expected VA 0x5FFAD0). At r=4 it tests this[22]==6/4=1, but with the P2 grouping client frames end at phases 2, 3, 5 and 6. So in the patch it stops firing entirely, rather than firing at a different boundary. sub_715070 looks like render-object cleanup (sub_9903B0/sub_994160, 20 slots per entry) and is probably client-only; its sim relevance is speculative.

(c) The strongest sim-visible item is the destroy-list shift, so the 'finding' should say so. processDestroyList runs at the 5|6 boundary instead of the 6|1 boundary. That changes both the bucket-3 order and how long destroyed objects live, relative to phase-6 bucket-3 updates and the next logic frame's phase-1 object walk (sub_78E560).

summary: I checked every instruction that references the four rewritten derived globals (refs.py, grouped by function): flt_CDBC50 has 15 reader functions (plus its initializer, which also feeds the 1/fps value), 0xCDBC54 has 9, flt_CDBC5C has 8 and flt_CDBD34 has 7. One real simulation hazard turned up, and the earlier 'client-side or self-consistent' verdict on flt_CDBC50 is wrong for it. When a unit switches locomotor, its height eases from the old height to the new one. The code sets the length of that ease to flt_CDBC50 * 0.5 steps (sub_73ABC0 @0x0073AC7C) and counts it down by 1 per locomotor update (sub_715ED0 @0x00715FD9, sub_778AA0 @0x00778B4B). That update runs once per LOGIC frame, reached from AIUpdate::update (sub_7DCFD0), and the result is written into the Object's position z. So the ease lasts 15 logic frames on a 30 fps machine, 30 at 60 fps and 45 at 90 fps. For the same logic frame, a 30 fps player and a 90 fps player compute different z values. In the ancestor engine (Generals), Object::crc includes the full transform matrix, so this should desync on the first locomotor switch where the height changes, for example an amphibious unit going between land and water. This matches all three measurements: replays desync only when FL_G_DER_FPS is on and the target is 60, the patch at target 30 does not desync, and live MP between 30 and 90 fps desyncs. It has not been proven to be source I or source II. Background: the four globals are RA3's copies of the Generals constants LOGICFRAMES_PER_SECONDS_REAL, MSEC_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL, LOGICFRAMES_PER_MSEC_REAL and SECONDS_PER_LOGICFRAME_REAL (GameCommon.h:75-78), all built from the old value 30. RA3 moved nearly all simulation code to flt_CDBC58 = (float)CAF9D0 = 15 (initializer at 0x00BB30A6, about 700 references, not rewritten by the patch). The locomotor ease is a leftover simulation reader of the 30-based constant. Every other reader of the four globals works in display-frame units on client objects: Drawable fade and tint, W3D visuals, LaserUpdate, particles, EVA, audio, music conditions, camera and UI. That leaves two low-confidence leaks, listed in open_questions.

verified.title: Locomotor height-transition ramp length = flt_CDBC50*0.5 LOGIC frames -> sim z-position depends on local fps (15/30/45 frames at 30/60/90)
verified.mechanism: Countdown initialised: sub_73ABC0 (dump 699121; line 699169 `*(float*)(v7+88) = flt_CDBC50*0.5`), disasm 0x0073AC71 `mov esi,[esi+0x21C]` (AIUpdate current locomotor) ; 0x0073AC7C `movss xmm0,[0xCDBC50]` ; 0x0073AC84 `mulss xmm0,[0xBE6678]` (=0.5) ; 0x0073AC8C `movss [esi+0x58],xmm0`. Old locomotor's (offset+preferredHeight) is copied to new.+0x50 at 0x0073AC77. Consumers: sub_715ED0 (dump 668216) and sub_778AA0 (dump 748994): `off = (start - preferred) / (flt_CDBC50*0.5) * countdown; countdown -= 1.0` (0x00715FD9 movss xmm4,[0xCDBC50]; 0x00715FE9 divss; 0x00715FF1 subss xmm1,[1.0]; 0x00716001 store [edi+0x58]), then z = off + preferredHeight + groundHeight (TheTerrainLogic dword_CE8F60 vtbl+36; sub_778AA0 also the water height sub_85A780). Call chain (all SIMULATION): sub_7DCFD0 = AIUpdate::update (in 10 vtables, e.g. 0x00C48910; returns 0x3FFFFFFF = UPDATE_SLEEP_FOREVER; this+540 = locomotor, this+8 = Object; dump 825047) -> sub_73ABC0 (line 825123) every update; and -> sub_7D8120 / sub_7D7BA0(locomotor, Object) (dump ~825138/825153) -> sub_78D510 (dump 765221; switch on locomotor template+96: case 0 -> sub_715ED0, case 1 -> sub_778AA0) -> writes Object+552/556/560 (x,y,z) and sets flag Object+566. Also sub_7A02F0 (Object+0x374 AI -> +0x21C loco -> sub_78D510(loco, Object, Object+56 position)) and sub_7A9750 (locomotor-set switch -> sub_73ABC0). The countdown goes down once per locomotor update (per logic frame), not per display frame. So the ramp length in logic frames is 0.5 x local flt_CDBC50: 15 at 30 fps, 30 at 60 fps, 45 at 90 fps. The prior pass's 'self-consistent, always 0.5 s' only holds if both sides counted display frames. Here the producer takes the local fps and the consumer counts logic frames, so machines at different fps compute different z on the same logic frame. Only transitions where old (offset+preferredHeight) != new preferredHeight are affected, likely amphibious land<->water switches (speculative as to which units).

Better long term, in line with the project's rule of redirecting readers rather than writing shared globals: stop rewriting the stored flt_CDBC50 and instead redirect only the verified client readers (sub_529F40, sub_542DF0, sub_5BF8A0, sub_5CC400, sub_6D7520, sub_6DCAE0, sub_783360, sub_903910 [already P6b], sub_90C3A0, sub_928990, sub_AC0070, sub_B19620) to g_fpsRender. Then no future unknown simulation reader can pick up the local fps. The fix is testable offline: a 30 fps replay under the 60/90 patch should stop desyncing when the first amphibious land<->water transition happens.
corrections:
These are minor precision points, none of which change the finding.

(a) The ramp does not start on every locomotor change. It starts only when current != previous and previous != NULL, and it has an effect only when old(+0x54 offset + +0x44 preferred height) != new +0x44. The finding says roughly this. Which units trigger it is still speculative; transforming units (ground/air or ground/hover locomotor swaps) are probably at least as likely as amphibious ones.

(b) The z divergence is transient. Once cnt <= 0 both machines zero the offset and z converges back to preferred + ground. Critical severity therefore depends on RA3's CRC including the Object transform (the SAGE ancestor Object::crc does, GeneralsMD Object.cpp:3913), or on some simulation decision reading z during the 15–45-frame window. Neither is proven for the RA3 binary. "likely" is the right confidence; "certain" is not.

(c) sub_78D510 also writes a pending position to Object+552..560 with z = 2*locoZ - Object+52 (the old transform z) and sets flag +566. Its only reader I found is sub_6FD340, a velocity estimate: (pending - pos) when +566 is set. That is a second simulation-visible channel for the same divergence.

(d) Dump line 748994 is the CDBC50 line inside sub_778AA0. The function itself starts at 748965.

(e) The long-term fix's list of "verified client readers" was not checked in this pass. sub_783360 (0x783360, in the locomotor/AI address range) builds an object through dword_CEDEC8 using flt_CDBC50 * v17 as frame counts, so check that it is client-side before redirecting it to g_fpsRender. The same applies to sub_6D7520 and sub_6DCAE0.

(f) I did not rule out other writers of locomotor+0x58 by a full scan. The only ones found are sub_73ABC0, sub_715ED0 and sub_778AA0, all on the logic path.

1) The mechanism and the three fix sites are correct. The operand bytes check out with refs.py: 0x0073AC7C F3 0F 10 05 50 BC CD 00 (operand at 0x0073AC80), 0x00715FD9 F3 0F 10 25 ... (0x00715FDD), 0x00778B4B F3 0F 10 1D ... (0x00778B4F).

2) Addition: the z reaches the simulation through sub_7D7BA0 -> sub_7C1300(Object, loco+112, flag) -> sub_7E35D0 = Object::setTransformMatrix (copies the matrix into Object+8 and position into Object+56..64). Object+552..560 is only a pending-position/velocity helper that sub_6FD340 reads. The main sink is the transform write, not +552.

3) Attribution to the measured desyncs: FL_G_DERIVED2 was on in every desync arm of RE-不同步诊断 §8.9/§8.10 (0x2CFFF, 0x2CFFE, 0x2CFE0, 0x2CE00). The arm with DERIVED2 off would not run. So this mechanism is independent of FL_G_RATIO and would show up as "source II" (~10800 frames in any config), not "source I". Speculative: it depends on when the replay first has a locomotor switch with a height difference.

4) Cadence evidence: the per-logic-frame claim holds through the scheduler semantics in sub_4F81F0 (a module is called only when module+4 <= TheGameLogic+80, and rescheduled to at least now+1). The concrete vtable slot that routes sub_4F81F0 to sub_7DCFD0 is not identified. The 10 vtable hits sit at an apparent slot 244 (+0x3D0), and I found no call through +0x3D0 and no adjustor thunk. The boundaries of these vtables are unclear because there is no RTTI.

5) The fix is right to pin the producer and both consumers together to 30.0f. Pinning only some of them would create a producer/consumer mismatch.

(a) sub_73ABC0 runs on every AIUpdate update, but it writes the countdown only when the current locomotor changes and the previous one was non-null (dump 699146-699169: `if (v2 != result) { ... if (v2) { v7+80 = old+84 + old+68; v7+88 = flt_CDBC50*0.5; } }`). It is not rewritten every update.
(b) The affected units are no longer speculative. template+96 is the LocoZ BehaviorZ enum, so case 0 = NO_MOTIVE_FORCE (ground) and case 1 = SEA_LEVEL. The official Locomotor.xml lists 10 SEA_LEVEL water locomotors with non-zero PreferredHeight, from -12 to +5: HumanWater -1, HumanWalkOnWater -2, AlliedScoutInfantryWater -2, AlliedAntiNavyShipTech1Water -10, SovietMCVWater -10, SovietSurveyorWater -12, SovietAntiAirShipWater -7, SovietAntiStructureShipWater +5, SovietScoutVehicleWater +1, JapanAntiVehicleVehicleTech1_Water -4. Ground locomotors are 0. So the swimming-infantry and amphibious-vehicle templates in that list start a ramp whenever they switch between land and water, in either direction. Unit names are inferred from template ids.
(c) Vanilla ramp length is 15 logic frames = 1.0 s (not 0.5 s). Patched it is 2 s at 60 fps and 3 s at 90 fps.
(d) Two points to add to the evidence and severity. First, the result is committed to the Object transform at 0x007D83B5 (sub_7ADF20) or 0x007D83C7 (sub_7E35D0), with ecx = the Object. Second, the divergence is temporary (at most 45 logic frames per switch, then the offset is reset to exactly 0). It shows up as a desync only if RA3's CRC hashes the transform in that window or if z feeds another simulation decision then. The Zero Hour ancestor's Object::crc hashes the transform; for RA3 this is not verified. The engine's own desync dump (HANDOFF line 203, poke 0xCAFF78) on the frame right after a unit enters water would confirm it.
(e) The fix operand addresses are correct: 0x0073AC80, 0x00715FDD and 0x00778B4F, with instruction bytes F3 0F 10 05/25/1D 50 BC CD 00 as proposed.
